title: Learning trumpet from Chris Kelly and leading his own bands
summary: Kelly taught him trumpet from about 1918, took him on parades including Zulu; Stevenson bought his own horn, formed a band at 21, then a touring band in Mississippi.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: That's right, that's right. And, uh, and also my boy, I always say I want to play music. And, uh, when I got in age around about, uh, 18, well I'd registered to go to the First World War, but I was too young, I was in that last draft, 18 to 45, and I just had made 19 years old. I got my card to go away on the 12th, and pieces clad on the 11th. So when Chris Kelly came up to service, that's why I'd taken up music, I started, he taught me on trumpet. And, uh, later, when I come in, it's getting better and better, he used to take me on parades with him. I played, uh, in the Zulu's parade with him, Iron Percy Humphrey, that was during around 19, 19, 22. He played for the Zulu's. And later on, he used to send me on different jobs, I used to play. And, uh, and I was getting so good, and, uh, the first song he taught me was Margie. And the next song he taught me was Hold Me.
Well, did we get on what instrument you started on?
Trumpet. You started on trumpet too?

No, that wasn't my father's horn, that was the horn I bought. I bought it myself, I bought it from the Duke and Music store. Oh yeah, at the Nile Street. Yeah, Duke and Music store. And, uh, so Kelly used to take me everywhere he used to go, you know. And so later on I got, got up around about 19, say about 19 years old. And, uh, uh, no not 19 years old, I was 21 and I made my own band. Uh, me, Sammy Penn, not Sammy Penn, Sammy, uh, uh, William on trombone. And we had another, uh, fellow by the name of Mooka. George, George John was his name. He was called him Mooka. He was the drummer. And another fellow by the name of Everest Brown. He used to play clarinet. And we had another, another fellow playing, uh, banjo called Oliver. Oliver was the banjo player. And we had another fellow who was playing, uh, bass. Old man Tom Harris. He used to play bass with us. And, uh, so later on I come into getting better and better. And I made up another band. In Hosey. First time. Hosey. Hosey Harris. Hosey Harris. Bass player. He's in California now. And, uh, Jesse, Jesse Charles. He was on clatter. He was playing clatter at the time. Another fellow playing second trumpet by the name of Lacroix. And we had, uh, Charlie Hampton on piano. And Joe Phillip on guitar. We was traveling then. We traveled off to Mississippi. McCorm. See, McCorm was our head porter. And, uh, we traveled off to, uh, Magnolia, Lomerton, Hattisberg, Christian Spring. Traveled off to that playing. So, I came back to New Orleans. And that's where, uh, during WPA time, we made up a band. Me and George Lewis, we played down Decatur Street.
